gpu.note: h2d_gbps = idle-host copy-engine ceiling (N106 h2d_test, anon THP -> VRAM, exact); 23.9 GB/s with slot A busy (b70-microbench-2026-10-07)

nvme.name: 4x Samsung 9100 PRO 1TB RAID0 (md127, 512K chunk, XFS)
nvme.note: box-level array numbers; the B70 slot B container is capped at 6 GiB/s (docker --device-read-bps /dev/md127:6gb -> cgroup io.max 9:127 rbps=6442450944, verified to apply to the md device)

ceilings.vram_note: 256-bit GDDR6 19 Gbps peak; measured = weight bytes / time of the exl3xpu decode MoE kernel on GLM-5.3-Flash blobs (8-64 unique 9.47 MB experts per call, 413-461 GB/s); Qwen 1.86 MB blobs stream at 300-397 GB/s (smaller work-groups)
ceilings.pcie_note: X.memcpy_async on the compute queue, slot A busy. H2D from pinned USM: 22.0-24.3 GB/s batched at every size; single copy 0.127 ms (1.86 MB Qwen expert), 0.447 ms (9.47 MB GLM expert). From anon / memfd THP system pointers (SVM keys on): 14 GB/s batched at 1.86 MB, 19 at 9.47 MB, 22-24 at 64-256 MiB; single 0.21-0.23 / 0.69-0.72 ms. D2H is the weak direction: 7.0-8.6 GB/s to USM or THP at >= 9.47 MB, 3.6-4.5 GB/s at 1.86 MB to THP. Idle-host H2D 26.7 (N106).
ceilings.zerocopy_note: device kernel (exl3xpu MoE decode) reading expert blobs in host RAM over PCIe: 21.5-25.6 GB/s, pinned USM = memfd THP via xe SVM within noise; link-bound, so a RAM-resident expert costs bytes / ~23 GB/s
ceilings.nvme_note: slot B, 30 GB O_DIRECT reads of 9.47 MB GLM records, 32 threads: 6.49 GB/s read-only, 5.77 GB/s with the H2D copy pipelined (memfd THP ring -> VRAM); 1.86 MB Qwen records: 3.99 / 2.64 GB/s (Python thread pool on 4 cores is the limit, not the device). Bursts under ~1 s exceed the cap (blk-throttle slice credit: 7.2 GB/s for 8 GB). O_DIRECT into Level Zero USM host memory fails with EFAULT: records must land in anon/memfd pages (then SVM read or sysptr H2D)
ceilings.ddr_note: same host as omarchy-rtx3090-nvx4 (8ch DDR4-3200); slot B owns cpuset 44-47 and 32 GB
